decisions.reason: The preceding sentence already defines a closed record as one with no matter crossing, but the class clause only says contains only records satisfying the energy conditions, without explicitly requiring closure or giving sufficient membership conditions. This is a real definitional ambiguity, rather than a demonstrated false first-law deduction: the first-law carrier separately excludes matter exchange. Repaired by making membership exactly closed admitted records with the stated positive fixed mass, endpoint data and zero-change conditions; no matter may cross throughout the interval, even if its net transfer would be zero.

reviews.reason: Checked the typed process tuple, endpoint map conditions, lack of imposed trajectory regularity, boundary classification, fixed-chart kinetic-energy definition, SI convention and exact set/function suppliers. Core membership now explicitly requires closure and all endpoint energy data, taking an absent separately tracked potential term as zero. Protocol Q and W_on are declared on all admitted P_s and restricted to the same core class for closed bookkeeping; the adiabatic predicate is therefore typed on every admitted record. This defines model data, without proving realizability or extending the first-law balance to open or omitted-energy records. All 15 direct item uses and the owning page were examined. This is a native review of my own repair, not an independent review or certification.

exact_snippets: Fix two members $a=(c_A,x_A)$ and $b=(c_B,x_B)$, named constituents $A,B$ of those constitutions, and a declared contact-protocol convention. A **thermal-contact protocol** is an admitted preparation/process record $P$ of their compound system $A\sqcup B$, with the configuration curve $z_P:I_P\to Z_{A\sqcup B}$ and equilibrium endpoint configurations specified in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. The contact model supplies constituent endpoint-coordinate maps

and requires $\xi_A(z_P(t_0))=x_A$ and $\xi_B(z_P(t_0))=x_B$. These constituent maps are additional declared model data; they are not inferred from the compound's coordinate tuple. Write $x_A^+=\xi_A(z_P(t_1))$ and $x_B^+=\xi_B(z_P(t_1))$ for the constituent final coordinates. The two constituents are separated by a declared diathermal contact: matter transfer and mechanical or composition work across that contact are forbidden, while the protocol permits thermal energy transfer between the constituents. The compound's external boundary and all retained constraints are specified as in [[def-td-system-and-permitted-exchanges]] and [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. No continuity or differentiability of the configuration curve is added here.

Let $\mathcal P_T(A,B)$ be the set of contact records admitted by the fixed convention. The model supplies an internal transfer map $q_{A\to B}:\mathcal P_T(A,B)\to\mathbb R$, whose values are numerical magnitudes in joules: $q_{A\to B}[P]>0$ means net thermal energy transferred from $A$ to $B$ across this contact during $I_P$. Set $q_{B\to A}[P]:=-q_{A\to B}[P]$. Zero net internal heat transfer means exactly $q_{A\to B}[P]=0$; it does not assert zero transfer at every intermediate time. This map is additional protocol data, distinct from the compound's external-boundary map $Q$ in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. In particular, an isolated compound may have nonzero $q_{A\to B}$ while its external $Q$ is zero. Identifying this internal map with constituent heat records requires separately supplied constituent records and consistent boundary assignments.

$$P=(I,x^-,x^+,z,\kappa,b,r),$$
where $I=[t_0,t_1]$, $t_0<t_1$, is a finite time interval in seconds, $x^-\in X_\Gamma$, $x^+\in X_{\Gamma'}$, $z:I\to Z_\alpha$, $z(t_0)\in Z^-_\alpha$, $z(t_1)\in Z^+_\alpha$, $\xi^-_\alpha(z(t_0))=x^-$, $\xi^+_\alpha(z(t_1))=x^+$, $\kappa\in\mathcal K_\alpha$, $b\in\mathcal B_\alpha$, and $r\in\mathcal R_\alpha$. exact_snippets:
Let $P_s\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ be an admitted closed system process record as defined in [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], with system endpoints $x_{P_s}^-,x_{P_s}^+\in D_c$. Let $R$ be its ideal thermal reservoir and $B$ its ideal pressure store; both lie inside a declared isolated-compound outer boundary. Let $\widehat P\in\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s\sqcup R\sqcup B)$ be an admitted core closed process record for that isolated compound, whose supplied total mass is positive, whose endpoint center-of-mass velocities are defined in one fixed Galilean chart, and whose compound center-of-mass kinetic and separately tracked external-field potential energies have zero endpoint change. These are conditions on the whole compound, additional to the system-record conditions. By an extension, require that $\widehat P$ has the same time interval, system endpoints, system configuration path, and system-side protocol and transfer records as $P_s$, together with the reservoir and store records. Write its compound endpoint association as
$$
\rho_{\widehat P}(\pm)=(x_{P_s}^\pm,y_R^\pm,y_B^\pm)\in\mathcal F\subseteq D_c\times Y_R\times Y_B,
$$
where $Y_R,Y_B$ are the model-declared reservoir and store equilibrium state sets, represented as admitted constituent state domains (or subsets thereof) in the second-law endpoint split; $E_R,E_B$ and their entropies are the corresponding dimensioned state maps. The split is admitted as independent separated macroscopic systems by [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]]. The set $\mathcal F$ is the exact feasible endpoint set from [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. The system protocol assigns heat $Q[P_s]$ and work $W_{\rm on}[P_s]$ to $P_s$; the auxiliary endpoint changes in $\widehat P$ satisfy the reservoir and store relations in [A1]–[A2] below. No matter crosses the compound boundary, no work channel other than pressure-store work acts on the system, and no other energy-coordinate changes are omitted.

[F1] [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]: $P_s$ is one admitted closed system process record with endpoints $x_{P_s}^\pm$; its protocol assigns the same record's heat and work functionals $Q[P_s]$ and $W_{\rm on}[P_s]$ in joules. The isolated-compound record $\widehat P$ records the auxiliary endpoint states and extension of that system record.

exact_snippets: **Given:** The process and sign conventions of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], the closed-record first-law postulate [[post-td-first-law-energy]], and the stated ideal-gas model.
[F1] A process record is adiabatic exactly when $Q[P]=0$; $W_{\mathrm{on}}>0$ denotes work done on the system ([[def-td-process-and-protocol]]).

[A2] The gas is the system inside the declared outer boundary: no matter crosses it, its material constitution is fixed, and its mechanical model supplies a total mass $M>0$ and center-of-mass velocities in the fixed chart of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. The gas center of mass is at rest at both endpoint preparations, so $\Delta K_{\mathrm{cm}}=0$; no separately tracked external-field potential energy changes (the model may take that term to be absent), so $\Delta U_{\mathrm{ext}}=0$. Thus the admitted record is in $\mathcal P_{\mathrm{cl}}(s)$ as defined by [[def-td-process-and-protocol]]. Its protocol has $Q[P]=0$, a constant external load $p_f$ during compression, and $W_{\mathrm{on}}[P]=p_f(V_i-V_f)$. The final equilibrium obeys $p_fV_f=nRT_f$, and the initial equilibrium obeys $p_iV_i=nRT_i$. The apparatus is stipulated to dissipatively settle and to have zero entropy change.
